The '''52nd Academy Awards''' ceremony, organized by the [[Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences]] (AMPAS), honored [[1979 in film|films released in 1979]] and took place on April 14, 1980, at the [[Dorothy Chandler Pavilion]] in Los Angeles, beginning at 6:00&nbsp;p.m. [[Pacific Time Zone|PST]] / 9:00&nbsp;p.m. [[Eastern Time Zone|EST]]. During the ceremony, AMPAS presented [[Academy Awards]] (commonly referred to as Oscars) in 22 categories. The ceremony, televised in the United States by [[American Broadcasting Company|ABC]], was produced by [[Howard W. Koch]] and directed by [[Marty Pasetta]].<ref name="Osborne 2013 413">{{harvnb|Osborne|2013|p=413}}</ref> Comedian and talk show host [[Johnny Carson]] hosted the show for the second consecutive year. Three days earlier, in a ceremony held at [[The Beverly Hilton]] in [[Beverly Hills, California]], on April 11, the [[Academy Scientific and Technical Awards]] were presented by hosts [[Cloris Leachman]] and [[William Shatner]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Past Scientific & Technical Awards Ceremonies|url=http://www.oscars.org/awards/scitech/pastawards.html|access-date=July 31, 2013 |publisher=[[Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140213185729/http://www.oscars.org/awards/scitech/pastawards.html|archive-date=February 13, 2014}}</ref>

''[[Kramer vs. Kramer]]'' won five awards, including [[Academy Award for Best Picture|Best Picture]], [[Academy Award for Best Director|Best Director]] for [[Robert Benton]], [[Academy Award for Best Actor|Best Actor]] for [[Dustin Hoffman]], and [[Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress|Best Supporting Actress]] for [[Meryl Streep]]. [[Sally Field]] received [[Academy Award for Best Actress|Best Actress]] honors for ''[[Norma Rae]]'', and [[Melvyn Douglas]] won [[Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor|Best Supporting Actor]] for ''[[Being There]]''.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Harmetz |first1=Aljean |title=Oscars Won by ''Kramer'', Hoffman and Miss Field; ''All That Jazz'' Takes Craft Awards ''Kramer vs. Kramer'' Is the Oscar Leader 'New and Old Managements' Carson's 2d Year as Emcee Honorary Awards Streets Are Quieter |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1980/04/15/archives/oscars-won-by-kramer-hoffman-and-miss-field-all-that-jazz-takes.html |access-date=March 26, 2020 |work=The New York Times |url-access=limited |date=April 15, 1980 |archive-date=August 9, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200809112915/https://www.nytimes.com/1980/04/15/archives/oscars-won-by-kramer-hoffman-and-miss-field-all-that-jazz-takes.html |url-status=live }}</ref> The telecast received a mixed reception, with critics praising Carson's hosting performance but criticising the pacing and predictability of the ceremony. It garnered 49&nbsp;million viewers in the United States, which was a 6% increase from the previous year.

==Winners and nominees==
The nominees for the 52nd Academy Awards were announced on February 25, 1980, by Academy president [[Fay Kanin]] and actors [[Ed Asner]] and [[Yvette Mimieux]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Thomas |first1=Bob |title=''All That Jazz'', ''Kramer'' Lead Oscar Nominations |work=[[The Spokesman-Review]] |date=February 26, 1980 |page=14}}</ref> ''[[All That Jazz (film)|All That Jazz]]'' and ''[[Kramer vs. Kramer]]'' tied for the most nominations, with nine each.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Arnold |first1=Gary |title=''Kramer'' and ''Jazz'' . . . |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/lifestyle/1980/02/26/kramer-and-jazz/195f83c9-6436-44d1-9c64-84b95eb62143/ |access-date=February 15, 2020 |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |url-access=limited |date=February 26, 1980 |archive-date=August 4, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220804090339/https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/lifestyle/1980/02/26/kramer-and-jazz/195f83c9-6436-44d1-9c64-84b95eb62143/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The winners were announced at the awards ceremony on April 14. At age eight, Best Supporting Actor nominee [[Justin Henry]] became the youngest person nominated for an Oscar.<ref>{{harvnb|Kinn|Piazza|2002|p=219}}</ref>

===Honorary Awards===
* To [[Alec Guinness]] for advancing the art of screen acting through a host of memorable and distinguished performances.<ref name="HonoraryandSpecial"/>
* To Hal Elias for his dedication and distinguished service to the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences.<ref name="HonoraryandSpecial">{{cite web |title=Academy Awards Acceptance Speech Database |url=http://aaspeechesdb.oscars.org/results.aspx?QB5=AND&QF5=transcript+%7c+acceptorlink+%7c+ed+note+%7c+name+%7c+film+title+%7c+song+title+%7c+category+index+%7c+acceptor+statement+%7c+category+exact+%7c+name+authority+%7c+winner+statement+%7c+year+term&QI5=&QB1=AND&QF1=name+%7c+winner+statement+%7c+name+authority&QI1=&QB2=AND&QF2=film+title&QI2=&QB3=AND&QF3=category+index&QI3=&QB0=AND&QF0=year+term&QI0=%3d%221979+52nd%22&QF6=video+link&AC=QBE_QUERY&TN=aatrans&RF=WebReportList&DF=WebReportOscars&MR=0&BU=http%3a%2f%2faaspeechesdb.oscars.org%2findex.aspx& |publisher=Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences |access-date=March 26, 2020 |archive-date=August 4, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220804090331/http://aaspeechesdb.oscars.org/results.aspx?QB5=AND&QF5=transcript+%7C+acceptorlink+%7C+ed+note+%7C+name+%7C+film+title+%7C+song+title+%7C+category+index+%7C+acceptor+statement+%7C+category+exact+%7C+name+authority+%7C+winner+statement+%7C+year+term&QI5=&QB1=AND&QF1=name+%7C+winner+statement+%7C+name+authority&QI1=&QB2=AND&QF2=film+title&QI2=&QB3=AND&QF3=category+index&QI3=&QB0=AND&QF0=year+term&QI0=%3D%221979+52nd%22&QF6=video+link&AC=QBE_QUERY&TN=aatrans&RF=WebReportList&DF=WebReportOscars&MR=0&BU=http%3A%2F%2Faaspeechesdb.oscars.org%2Findex.aspx& |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Jean Hersholt Humanitarian Award===
The award recognizes individuals whose humanitarian efforts have brought credit to the motion picture industry.<ref>{{cite web |title=Jean Hersholt Humanitarian Award |url=https://www.oscars.org/governors/hersholt |publisher=Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences |access-date=12 November 2020 |archive-date=16 November 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201116224625/https://www.oscars.org/governors/hersholt |url-status=live }}</ref>

* [[Robert Benjamin]]<ref name="HonoraryandSpecial"/>

===Irving G. Thalberg Memorial Award===
The award honors "creative producers whose bodies of work reflect a consistently high quality of motion picture production".<ref>{{cite news|title=Irvin G. Thalberg Memorial Award |url=http://www.oscars.org/governors/thalberg |access-date=December 18, 2015 |publisher=Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160101224449/http://oscars.org/governors/thalberg |archive-date=January 1, 2016 }}</ref>

==Ceremony information==
[[File:Johnny Carson 1970.JPG|thumb|left|alt=A black-and-white photograph of Johnny Carson in 1970|[[Johnny Carson]] hosted the 52nd Academy Awards.]]

In September 1979, the academy hired film producer [[Howard W. Koch]] to produce the telecast for the sixth time.<ref>{{cite news |title=Koch Again |work=[[South Bend Tribune]] |date=September 30, 1979 |page=61}}</ref> Upon being named producer, Koch responded in a press release, stating, "I plan to involve all the professional and creative talents of the motion picture community in this program, as the Academy Awards, in the public's mind, represents the entire field of filmmaking."<ref>{{cite web |title=Howard W. Koch to Produce 52nd Annual Oscar Show |url=https://digitalcollections.oscars.org/digital/collection/p15759coll9/id/12210/rec/6 |publisher=Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences |access-date=July 13, 2022 |date=September 7, 1979 |archive-date=August 4, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220804090333/https://digitalcollections.oscars.org/digital/collection/p15759coll9/id/12210/rec/6 |url-status=live }}</ref> Two months later, it was announced that comedian and ''[[The Tonight Show Starring Johnny Carson|The Tonight Show]]'' host [[Johnny Carson]] would preside over emceeing duties for the 1980 ceremony.<ref>{{cite news |title=Carson to Host Show |work=[[Reno Gazette-Journal]] |date=November 27, 1979 |page=10}}</ref> "Johnny Carson is one of our national treasures. He was selected as this year's host because his wit and verve made him an outstanding master of ceremonies at last year's show," said Koch in a statement justifying his selection for host.<ref>{{cite web |title=Johnny Carson Set As Master of Ceremonies for 52nd Annual Academy Awards |url=https://digitalcollections.oscars.org/digital/collection/p15759coll9/id/12223/rec/6 |publisher=Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences |access-date=July 13, 2022 |date=November 6, 2013 |archive-date=July 14, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220714074942/https://digitalcollections.oscars.org/digital/collection/p15759coll9/id/12223/rec/6 |url-status=live }}</ref>

[[Marty Pasetta]] directed the telecast.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Boyer |first1=Peter J. |title=Marty Pasetta Has Hopes for a Lively Oscar Show |work=[[The Baltimore Sun]] |date=April 14, 1980 |page=B6}}</ref> [[Henry Mancini]] served as musical director and conductor for the ceremony, where he conducted an overture performed by the orchestra at the beginning of the show.<ref name="Osborne 2013 413"/> A song-and-dance number featuring actor and singer [[Donald O'Connor]] paid tribute to choreography in film.<ref>{{harvnb|Wiley|Bona|1996|p=580}}</ref>

===Critical reviews===
The ceremony received a mixed reception from critics. ''[[The Arizona Republic]]'' columnist Michael Maza wrote, "Watching last night's 52nd Annual Academy Award ceremonies was like sitting through three hours and 15 minutes of near-flawless close order drill. It wasn't long before the feet seemed to blur."<ref>{{cite news |last1=Maza |first1=Michael |title=Ho-Hum Oscars Was a 'Bowling Boquet of Stars' |work=[[The Arizona Republic]] |date=April 15, 1980 |page=B5}}</ref> Jack Mathews of the ''[[Detroit Free Press]]'' commented, "In any event, the 52nd Academy Awards presentation will stand as one of the smoothest, most predictable, and most reasonable Oscar nights in history. Also, alas, one of the most boring."<ref>{{cite news |last1=Mathews |first1=Jack |title=How Divorce, War and Death Can Turn Into a Big Yawner |work=[[Detroit Free Press]] |date=April 15, 1980 |page=12C}}</ref> ''[[The Baltimore Sun]]'' television critic Bill Carter quipped, "We found out Monday night when this year's edition of the Oscarcast streamlined to the point of emaciation (and still more than three hours long), thudded along like some awards dinner of the meat-packing industry." He praised Carson's hosting performance, but said, "For all the excitement this parade of stars provided, they might as well have sent in their stand-ins, or maybe some robot, or well dressed mannequins from a boutique on [[Rodeo Drive]]. This just wasn't a little boring, this was mind-numbingly boring."<ref>{{cite news |last1=Carter |first1=Bill |title=Oscarcast Without Silliness: How Boring |work=The Baltimore Sun |date=April 16, 1980 |page=B4}}</ref>

Others received the broadcast more positively. ''[[Los Angeles Times]]'' film critic [[Charles Champlin]] mused, "As a show, the Marty Pasetta-Howard Koch special revealed again a gift for all that pizzazz." He added, "If nobody in fact was dozing, it was thanks to Carson's own relaxed and engaging presence. Among his virtues, he is an emcee who seems to love the movies."<ref>{{cite news |last1=Champlin |first1=Charles |title=The Oscar Derby: A Horse Race After All |work=Los Angeles Times |date=April 16, 1980 |page=100}}</ref> Film critic [[Gene Siskel]] from the ''[[Chicago Tribune]]'' commented,  "The show was a visual delight, thanks to special electronic effects that presented scenes from each nominated film as its title was announced."<ref>{{cite news |last1=Siskel |first1=Gene |title=Oscars to Field, Hoffman, ''Kramer'' |work=[[Chicago Tribune]] |date=April 15, 1980 |pages=14}}</ref> Columnist Patrick Taggart of the ''[[Austin American-Statesman]]'' wrote, "Aren't we entitled to at least one upset victory among the nominees? The 52nd running of the Academy Awards was distinguished by the utter lack of any such color; but somehow, in spite of its slickness, Monday's show was a relatively good one."<ref>{{cite news |last1=Taggart |first1=Patrick |title=Awards Show Sailed on Calm Waters |work=[[Austin American-Statesman]] |date=April 16, 1980 |page=E7}}</ref>

===Ratings and reception===
The American telecast on ABC drew in an average of 49&nbsp;million people over the length of the entire ceremony, which was a 6% increase from the [[51st Academy Awards|previous year's ceremony]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Consoli |first1=Jon |title=Spotlight's on Oscars But for ABC, Ratings Wins Begin on Red Carpet |url=https://www.nexttv.com/news/spotlights-oscars-abc-ratings-wins-begin-red-carpet-114164 |access-date=April 16, 2022 |work=[[Broadcasting & Cable]] |date=February 21, 2013 |archive-date=April 21, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210421214412/https://www.nexttv.com/news/spotlights-oscars-abc-ratings-wins-begin-red-carpet-114164 |url-status=live }}</ref> However, the show drew lower [[Nielsen ratings]] compared to the previous ceremony, with 33.7% of households watching with a 55% share.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Margulies |first1=Lee |url=https://latimes.newspapers.com/newspage/385269732/ |title=Ratings Race a Photo Finish? |work=Los Angeles Times |date=April 18, 1980 |page=119 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{subscription required}}</ref> Furthermore, the ceremony presentation received five nominations at the [[32nd Primetime Emmy Awards|32nd Primetime Emmys]], but failed to win any of its nominations.<ref>{{cite web |title=Primetime Emmy Awards Database |url=https://www.emmys.com/shows/52nd-annual-awards-presentation-academy |publisher=[[Academy of Television Arts and Sciences]] |access-date=March 26, 2020 |archive-date=March 3, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210303211653/https://www.emmys.com/shows/52nd-annual-awards-presentation-academy |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine |title=Academy of TV Arts & Sciences 1979-80 Emmy Nominations |magazine=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |volume=262 |issue=48 |date=Aug 8, 1980 |pages=5, 29 |id={{ProQuest|2598133563}}}}</ref>
